content:
maddie: Quick follow-up from the precision profiles RFC — couple of runtime/contract items we didn't close. Need to align on handshake, telemetry keys, and fallback semantics before the canary.
thomas: SG. Which handshake bits are blocking you? schema? versioning? runtime negotiation?
maddie: All of the above. Specifically:
  1) How the client (controller) advertises supported precisions to the runtime (FP8, INT8, INT4, mixed per-layer)
  2) What the runtime returns when it declines a profile (error vs suggested alternative)
  3) How we mark cache/kvkey compatibility when precision changes
anya: Also, don't forget calibration sets. If a profile implies different calibration, we must surface that in rollout metrics.
simon: Telemetry: we need precision-specific buckets for latency/cost/quality. Otherwise it's impossible to correlate degradation to a precision switch.
chen: For fallback semantics I'd favour a deterministic fallback chain, not a black-box negotiation. Example: requested->fp8, fallback->int8, fallback->fp16. Keep it explicit so upper layers can plan.
nate: Agreed. Also add a profile id/version so serving can evict caches when the profile changes. Maybe a short hash in response headers like `x-precision-profile: pp-v2-1a2b`.
maddie: Proposal sketch:
```
POST /infer
Body: { model: "rw-causal-7b", precision_profile: "pp-v2-1a2b" }
Response: { accepted_profile: "pp-v2-1a2b", actual_precision: "int8", fallback_chain: ["fp8","int8","fp16"], cache_key_version: "ckv-7" }
```
thomas: I like explicit fields. Two follow-ups:
  - Do we allow profile negotiation (server suggests acceptable profiles) or only accept/deny?
  - How does this interact with router policies (cost-first vs latency-first)?
anya: We should allow server suggestions but keep client choice. Router can pick route based on policy then the runtime can reply with a suggested alternative if it can't serve the requested profile.
simon: For metrics, add per-request tags: precision_requested, precision_actual, profile_id, fallback_step. That lets us slice quality evals against each transition.
chen: For caching: if actual_precision != requested_precision we must invalidate any prefix cache entries keyed only by model+input. Solution: include profile_id+precision_actual in cache key. TTLs may differ by precision too.
nate: Ops note: canary must include synthetic eval set with prompts that are sensitive to quantization artifacts. We need threshold alerts (e.g., BLEU or factuality delta) and automatic rollback trigger.
ops-bot: Canary scheduled: infra/canary-runner will run v2 precision canary at 2026-04-02T03:00Z. Notifications to #eng-ml and #eng-sre.
maddie: Edge cases:
  - Per-layer overrides: allow them but treat them as part of profile id (so cache/versioning handles it)
  - Mixed-precision in multi-GPU routing: require deterministic mapping to avoid divergence
  - API backward compatibility: if no profile provided, behaviour unchanged (default profile)
thomas: Implementation plan:
  - API & runtime changes (2 sprint)
  - Telemetry schema updates + dashboards (1 sprint)
  - Canary + eval harness (1 sprint)
chen: Also add linting to profile uploader to prevent profiles that set incompatible kernel combos for a given model.
anya: We'll attach a short calibration manifest with each profile: calibration_set_id and a small checksum so ops can verify calibration artifact existence.
simon: And emit a small "quality_delta" metric post-request that compares on-the-fly evals for canary traffic.
maddie: OK this is actionable. Assigning:
  - thomas + chen = runtime + api
  - anya = calibration/eval sets
  - simon = telemetry/dashboards
  - nate = canary orchestration
I'll open the follow-up RFC PR with the handshake schema tonight.
thomas: Thanks — I'll review and add the fallback enum values.
chen: I'll prototype cache_key changes.
nate: Will wire canary runner.
ops-bot: Reminder: attach runbook entries for rollback triggers to the PR.
maddie: Perfect. If anyone has objections to the deterministic fallback enum please speak now, otherwise I'll proceed.
simon: :+1:
anya: +1
thomas: +1
chen: +1
nate: +1
maddie: Great — closing on this thread, will ping when PR is up.
